question: What is the primary objective of health care financing?

options.A: Eliminating the need for government involvement in hospitals
options.B: Maximizing profit generation for private pharmaceutical companies
options.C: Reducing the total number of healthcare workers in public facilities
options.D: Ensuring access to necessary services without financial hardship

explanation: Health financing aims to fund health systems so that people can receive needed care without being driven into poverty by medical bills. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why are heavy reliance on out-of-pocket payments problematic for a health system?

options.A: They make hospital administration completely transparent and corruption-free
options.B: They eliminate the need for any government budget allocation
options.C: They guarantee equal access to advanced surgical care for all citizens
options.D: They frequently cause catastrophic expenditures and impoverishment for households

explanation: Paying directly cash at the point of care prevents many poor individuals from seeking treatment and ruins family finances when severe illness strikes. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is the specific function of the 'pooling' component in health care financing?

options.A: Collecting taxes directly from corporate entities for road construction
options.B: Discharging patients who cannot pay their hospital bills
options.C: Accumulating financial resources to spread health risks across a population
options.D: Negotiating drug prices with international pharmaceutical manufacturers

explanation: Pooling combines funds so that the financial burden of illness is shared collectively rather than borne by the sick individual alone. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h2)

question: How does health care purchasing differ from revenue collection?

options.A: Purchasing involves paying providers for services using pooled funds, whereas collection gathers the money
options.B: Purchasing is done exclusively by international donors, whereas collection is done by nurses
options.C: Purchasing happens before revenue collection in every functioning health system
options.D: Purchasing refers to buying hospital land, whereas collection refers to buying medications

explanation: Revenue collection brings money into the system, while purchasing is the active allocation of those gathered funds to healthcare providers. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h2)

question: What characterizes social health insurance as a source of health care funds?

options.A: Completely voluntary monthly donations made by religious institutions
options.B: Direct cash payments made by patients at the pharmacy counter
options.C: Grants given exclusively by foreign humanitarian organizations
options.D: Mandatory payroll contributions tied to formal employment status

explanation: Social health insurance pools funds through compulsory contributions from workers and employers, often subsidized for the vulnerable. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h3)

question: A patient pays cash for consultation and drugs immediately after seeing a doctor. Which funding source does this represent?
explanation: Direct payments made by individuals at the time they receive care without third-party reimbursement are classified as out-of-pocket expenditures. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of risk pooling in a health system?

options.A: To spread the financial burden of illness across a larger group of people
options.B: To generate maximum profit for private hospital owners and investors
options.C: To eliminate the need for medical records in primary health centers
options.D: To ensure that doctors are paid based on the number of patients they turn away

explanation: Pooling distributes financial risk so that unexpected, high-cost medical needs do not bankrupt individual families. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which practice describes strategic purchasing in health care financing?

options.A: Allowing private clinics to set their own unregulated drug prices
options.B: Waiting until a hospital runs out of money before releasing government funds
options.C: Contracting providers based on quality and prioritizing cost-effective interventions
options.D: Reimbursing hospitals for every single test ordered regardless of clinical necessity

explanation: Strategic purchasing involves actively shaping how funds are spent to maximize health outcomes and efficiency rather than passive fee-for-service payment. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary body responsible for regulating health insurance and promoting universal coverage in Nigeria?

options.B: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing
options.C: World Health Organization African Regional Office

explanation: The NHIA is the statutory body charged with regulating, promoting, and integrating health insurance schemes across Nigeria. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h5)

question: A petty trader in a local Nigerian market has no formal employer and pays cash every time she visits a clinic. Which sector does her health financing profile represent?

options.B: The informal sector relying on out-of-pocket spending
options.C: The external donor-funded military health system
options.D: The formal sector under mandatory federal social insurance

explanation: Self-employed individuals in unstructured trades form the informal sector, which frequently lacks prepaid insurance and relies on direct out-of-pocket payments. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge of health care financing in many developing countries?

options.A: A massive, well-documented formal employment sector paying high payroll taxes
options.B: Low government budgetary allocation to the health sector
options.C: Heavy reliance on direct out-of-pocket spending by poor households
options.D: Vulnerability caused by a heavy dependence on external donor funds

explanation: Developing countries typically struggle with a large informal economy, making payroll tax collection difficult rather than having a well-documented formal sector. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h6)

question: How does a large informal sector negatively impact national health insurance schemes?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any primary healthcare facilities in rural areas
options.B: It generates so much excess tax revenue that governments stop prioritizing public health
options.C: It forces commercial insurance companies to lower their premium prices globally
options.D: It lacks fixed payrolls, making mandatory wage-based contributions difficult to track and collect

explanation: Because informal workers lack formal employers and regular salary slips, collecting systematic monthly insurance premiums presents a major logistical hurdle. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the core definition of Universal Health Coverage (UHC)?

options.A: Free medical care provided exclusively by foreign pharmaceutical companies
options.B: Mandatory hospitalization for every citizen at least once a year
options.C: The elimination of all private hospitals within a developing nation
options.D: Access to needed quality health services without financial hardship

explanation: UHC ensures that financial barriers do not prevent anyone from getting the promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative care they require. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h7)

question: Why is strengthening primary health care considered a critical strategy for achieving UHC?

options.A: It ensures that health financing relies entirely on out-of-pocket payments
options.B: It serves as a cost-effective first point of contact that addresses most community health needs
options.C: It removes the need for trained nurses and doctors in rural communities
options.D: It guarantees that every citizen will receive specialized open-heart surgery locally

explanation: Primary health care tackles common conditions close to where people live, preventing minor illnesses from escalating into expensive hospital emergencies. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h7)

question: How do bedside nurses directly impact health care costs and resource utilization?

options.A: By minimizing waste, preventing complications, and managing clinical supplies efficiently
options.B: By setting the national tax rates for corporate manufacturing companies
options.C: By collecting personal income taxes from informal market traders
options.D: By negotiating international trade agreements for medical equipment

explanation: Careful use of consumables and the prevention of hospital-acquired infections directly reduce the financial burden on both the facility and the patient. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h8)

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand health care financing principles?

options.A: It allows them to bypass hospital administrators and manage institutional budgets directly
options.B: It replaces their clinical training with advanced commercial banking skills
options.C: It ensures they can collect out-of-pocket cash payments from every patient
options.D: It enables them to advocate for resource equity and guide patients on using prepayment schemes

explanation: A grasp of financing empowers nurses to participate in health policy, support insurance enrollment, and make resource-conscious clinical decisions. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h8)
